task.name: A high preflight complexity score buys accommodation but never prompts a scope decision, so an over-broad story is planned at full cost
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2680
---

## Problem

Preflight scores a story's complexity for roughly $0.37 and forge then spends the
remaining 98% of the run not acting on that number. A high score buys longer timeouts
and stronger models; it never prompts a question. Issue #2541 scored 9, ran twice for
$43.64, and never reached DEV. It turned out to contain four independently deliverable
pieces of work, which landed for $86.11 once split — a judgment the operator made by
hand, after the money was spent, from evidence forge already had before planning began.

Cost is concentrated after the score is known. On the second #2541 run, preflight was
$0.37, planning $3.77, and plan review $29.25. Every dollar past preflight was spent on
a story the score had already flagged.

Human teams handle this with a soft ceiling: past some estimate, someone asks whether
the work should be split before it is planned in detail. The number is a rough up-front
judgment, not the product of deep analysis, and it triggers a conversation rather than
a refusal. Forge computes the equivalent number and discards its only cheap opportunity
to use it.

Forge has two existing scope refusals and neither has ever protected a run: the intake
cluster heuristic admitted #2541, and the planner's decompose signal has not fired in
any recorded run. A gate that ships inactive would be a third. This one is active by
default, with the threshold configurable in both directions.

Depends on #2680: the shipped default threshold must be chosen against the range of
scores that are actually reachable.

## What

At a configurable preflight complexity threshold, active by default, a run pauses
before it spends anything further and asks the operator to approve the story as scoped
or return it for decomposition.

## Scope: test isolation

Tests whose setup newly satisfies the production trigger may explicitly disable the
gate through test configuration, or supply a controlled decision, when the test is
not exercising gate behaviour. Those edits are test isolation, they are in scope, and
the general rule against modifying unrelated existing tests does not apply to them.

This permits nothing else. It is not licence to change production defaults, weaken
the production trigger, or alter the score or verdict a test is asserting on.

## Constraint

The production trigger is not narrowed to make the suite pass. The gate ships
default-on at its configured threshold and fires for every case the criteria below
describe; a predicate that suppresses it for cases those criteria include is a
change to the feature, not a fix to the tests, whatever its stated rationale. If
the suite cannot pass with the trigger intact, say so and stop rather than
adjusting what the gate does.

## Acceptance criteria

- A story whose preflight verdict is PROCEED and whose complexity score reaches the
  configured threshold blocks before any cost-bearing phase that follows preflight, and
  reports the score and the decision awaiting the operator. The gate is anchored to the
  end of preflight, not to any one downstream phase, so a story that skips planning
  because preflight classified it implementation-ready still stops here.
- A story whose preflight verdict is not PROCEED never blocks on this gate.
- The threshold is configurable and ships active with a default value. Raising the
  threshold above the highest score preflight can assign disables the gate; no separate
  enable switch exists, and a run with the shipped configuration emits the pause.
- An operator decision to approve logs the story as explicitly approved at that score,
  and the run continues exactly as it would have without the gate.
- An operator decision to decompose exits the run without spending on any later phase,
  and reports the story as returned for decomposition rather than as a story that
  failed.
- The pause is scoped to the story it applies to: it does not cancel or stop sibling
  stories already executing, and it does not affect a story that does not depend on it.
  Under forge's current operator-gate architecture the waiting story may retain its own
  worker slot until a decision or expiry, exactly as the existing operator gates do.
  Releasing that slot and durably re-dispatching the story are out of scope here and
  tracked in #2806.
- When no decision arrives within the configured wait, the run takes the configured
  no-decision action, which accepts only the same two values an operator may choose, and
  reports which action it took and that no operator decision was recorded. The shipped
  no-decision action returns the story for decomposition. Configuration that is absent,
  empty, or not one of the two accepted values also returns the story rather than
  proceeding, so no misconfiguration can spend on an unapproved story.

## Example

A sprint reaches the gate on a story scoring at the threshold. The decision is keyed by
the story's own run id, as reported by `forge status`, not by the sprint's:

```
▸ #2541  PREFLIGHT  complexity 9 (impl 9, validation 3)  — awaiting operator
  Threshold 9 (default). Nothing has been spent beyond preflight for this story.

    forge decide 7c1e04b9d3af approve      plan and implement it as scoped
    forge decide 7c1e04b9d3af decompose    return it to be split

  No decision within 30m: decompose (default). Stories on other workers are unaffected.
```

Approving proceeds unchanged and records the approval, so a large-but-cohesive story is
never blocked by its size alone. Returning it costs the $0.37 already spent on preflight
instead of the $43.64 that #2541 actually cost.

handoff.summary: Completed the preflight complexity gate (#2681). The gate is anchored at _handle_preflight_verdict — the single handoff every preflight path (fresh, cached, resumed) passes through — so a PROCEED verdict whose projected complexity score reaches the configured threshold pauses before any cost-bearing phase, including for implementation_ready stories that skip PLAN entirely. preflight_complexity_gate.py reuses the existing pending-decision primitives (bounded_gate_wait/write_pending/poll_pending/cleanup_pending) with options approve/decompose keyed by the STORY's run id. Config ships threshold 9 with no separate enable switch; a threshold above COMPLEXITY_SCORE_MAX disables it. normalize_preflight_gate_no_decision fails closed, resolving absent/empty/unrecognised no-decision config to decompose. A returned story becomes StoryOutcome.DECOMPOSED — terminal, outside the failed bucket, rendered '⤺ returned for decomposition' and dag.mark_skipped so dependents are not released. This run's contribution was verification plus test isolation: 7 tests asserting timeout/routing behaviour were newly tripping the production trigger and were isolated via threshold=11 in their local config builders, matching the established coord_test_helpers pattern. The production trigger was not narrowed.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2, advisory cleanup after APPROVE. Both carried P2s were one root cause: CHANGELOG.md and docs/guides/controller-runbook.md claimed only a preflight-founded score opens the complexity gate and that degraded/nothing-examined runs continue unasked, while should_gate() opens on any PROCEED score >= threshold. The code is correct — narrowing the trigger to founded scores would violate the story's constraint against suppressing the gate for cases the criteria include — so I rewrote both docs to present foundedness as context for the operator's decision rather than a suppression of it, and to state that opened:false now means exactly one thing (score under threshold, or gate disabled). Fixing the prose exposed the rejected design's live remnant: preflight_complexity_gate_withheld_reason was assigned None and never anything else, yet was plumbed through state.py, audit.py, resume_persistence.py and the v41 schema fixture behind an audit comment promising it marked withheld gates. Renamed it to preflight_complexity_gate_score_provenance and populated it from _score_provenance_note(), so the audit records the provenance the operator actually ruled on instead of a permanently-null field; the v41 schema is introduced by this branch and unreleased, so no migration is required. Gate runtime behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

finding_registry.description: The release notes and controller runbook state that degraded or nothing-examined high complexity scores continue without opening the gate, while the runtime gate and tests open the gate for those scores.

The CHANGELOG states "Only a score preflight actually founded opens it: a degraded attempt...those runs continue unasked with withheld_reason on the audit," but the code in preflight_complexity_gate.py:128 gates on all scores >= threshold regardless of foundedness, and test_unfounded_high_score_still_pauses_and_records_its_provenance confirms unfounded scores do open the gate.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
